To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the sharp and blunt egg poles of an egg differ in temperature, cooling rates, and the way they are oriented within a clutch.

egg surface temperature, and cooling rates differ significantly between the sharp and the blunt poles of the same egg and that the arrangement of eggs in an avian clutch can significantly affect the temperature and cooling rates of the whole clutch.

the sharp poles of the eggs warmed to a significantly higher temperature and cooled faster than did the blunt pole of the egg, and the eggs arranged in the clutch in the way that the sharp pole of the egg was directed towards the center of the clutch, had a significantly higher egg temperature than did the scattered eggs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the thermal ecology of eggs, which has important implications for understanding the evolution and ecology of avian reproduction.
the thermal properties of the egg and the way in which birds arrange their eggs within a clutch, which is important for the development of the embryo.
the thermoregulation mechanisms that are used by birds during incubation, and how the arrangement and orientation of eggs within the nest affects heat loss.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the arrangement of eggs in a clutch can influence heat transfer to and from eggs, with implications for the energetics of incubation.
the arrangement of eggs in an avian clutch can influence egg surface temperature and heat loss from the clutch.
the egg surface temperature and the cooling rate differ between the sharp pole and the blunt pole of the egg.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
birds have a number of different strategies to regulate temperature within the clutch, including egg turning, egg arrangement and egg orientation.
egg orientation in the clutch can influence the cooling pattern of eggs and clutches and thus may have implications for embryonic development.
egg surface temperature varies between the different areas of the egg and the arrangement of the eggs within the nest can affect the temperature of the clutch as whole.

the orientation of eggs within the nest affects the temperature distribution within the clutch and the overall cooling rate of the clutch.
the orientation of eggs in an avian clutch is important for thermoregulation.
egg surface temperatures are differentially distributed across the egg and that egg arrangement within the clutch affects cooling rates of the whole clutch.
